title: The independent reading of the 46 newly captured Zoning Resolution texts into the R6B reference cases (mixed-building floor area ZR 35-30 to 35-33, with 35-31's paragraph on floor area shared by several uses; the definition of floor area ratio; ZR 23-24 and ZR 34-23; the ZR 12-10 definitions 'fully electrified building', 'ultra low energy building', 'building' and 'story'; and fourteen sections on whether parking, loading berths and bicycle parking are required), plus the benchmark lot's rear yard read from ZR 23-342 and 23-344; with one mixed building worked by hand and a parking/loading/bicycle line per development option; it writes reference rows and worked examples only and changes NO rule file, NO engine code, NO result, NO register entry and NO capture, and enters NO human verdict anywhere [DB-184 first piece; DB-185 (b); D-090 R291, R513, R516, R526, R548]
objective: Read independently the 46 official Zoning Resolution texts captured by tasks M4-T033 and M4-T034 (docs/research/zr-snapshots/v1/) that no reference case has yet read, and write what the two readings settle into the R6B reference cases as a new step-P5 case. Backlog row DB-184 (first piece) and DB-185 (b) name what is owed. The six text groups to read: (1) the mixed-building floor-area sections ZR 35-30, 35-31, 35-32 and 35-33, where 35-31 itself holds the paragraph on floor area shared by several uses ('the #floor area# for such shared portion shall be attributed to each #use# proportionately'), together with the ZR 12-10 definition of floor area ratio (zr-12-10-floor-area-ratio); (2) the ZR 12-10 energy definitions 'fully electrified building', 'ultra low energy building', 'building' and 'story'; (3) ZR 23-24 (special provisions for certain areas) and ZR 34-23 (modification of yard regulations, with its sub-section list zr-34-23-contents); (4) the fourteen sections on whether parking, loading berths and bicycle parking are REQUIRED (zr-25-02, zr-25-20, zr-25-211, zr-25-221, zr-25-231, zr-25-80, zr-25-81, zr-25-811, zr-36-21, zr-36-31, zr-36-62, zr-36-70, zr-36-71, zr-36-711); (5) one mixed building worked by hand; (6) the benchmark lot's rear yard read from ZR 23-342 and 23-344 (DB-185 (b)). INPUT MADE BY THE ORCHESTRATOR BEFORE THE BUILDER STARTS: two readings by two different AI helpers that took no part in writing the program's rules, each working alone from a sealed folder (all pinned law captures without their notes, the benchmark lot's recorded official facts and outline, and made-up lots, with no access to the program, the repository or the web). STEP 1: save the two returns unchanged under docs/reference-cases/R6B/provenance/ as return-independent-hand-calculation-11.md and return-independent-hand-calculation-12.md, each with a short header, and pin each file's digest. STEP 2: write the step-P5 reading into docs/reference-cases/R6B/cases/step-p5-worked.json (and its rendered page step-p5-worked.md), following the form of cases/step-p4-worked.json. Record a value or a yes/no ONLY where BOTH readings give it on the same basis; everywhere else record 'not sure'/'not known' with the reason and both readings named, and name what would settle it. Where one reading attaches a condition the other does not, state that condition in the value. Where a new row gives the current answer to a question an older row holds, mark the older row superseded_by the new row and never leave two current answers for one question; the known candidates are cases/step-p4-worked.json row made-up-100x100-units (held by both step-P4 readings subject to the floor-area-ratio definition they did not have, which is now captured) and cases/step-p3-worked.json row real-lot-rear-yard-beyond-corner (the current head of the benchmark rear-yard chain). Change an existing row's expected value or kind only where both readings support it, with a dated change-log entry. Say 'the readers did not have' a text outside their folder and 'not read by reading N' for a text in the folder a reader chose not to read; never 'not captured'. Update docs/reference-cases/R6B/README.md with a step-P5 section and its 'did not have' list; re-render the pages; extend the test support only as the new rows need (new modules r6b_reference_cases_step_p5.py and test_r6b_reference_cases_step_p5.py, modelled on the step-P4 pair; add 'step-p5-worked' to r6b_reference_cases_lib.py CASE_IDS and REQUIRED_BASE_IDS and wire the step-P5 guards into r6b_reference_cases_check.py; r6b_reference_cases_render.py only if a new row shape needs it). THE MIXED BUILDING WORKED BY HAND (group 5): one made-up mixed building (residential plus a commercial or community-facility use), worked from ZR 35-31's own words to show how the floor areas of the uses combine and how shared floor area is attributed proportionately; said to be made up; no value from a program run. THE PARKING, LOADING AND BICYCLE LINE PER OPTION (group 4): for each development option, state from the captured text what the line MAY say (either the applicability resolved from a captured provision, or 'not yet checked'/'not sure' naming the missing fact, e.g. the lot's transit zone, which the captured residential sections 25-211/221/231 turn on) and what it MAY NOT say (it may not declare an option feasible, may not state a count, and may not turn a question of law into the owner's preference). THE REAR-YARD READING OF THE BENCHMARK LOT (group 6): state the conditions of the waiver from the captured text of ZR 23-344(a) (no rear yard required within 100 feet of the point where two street lines meet at 135 degrees or less) and ZR 23-342 (the interior-lot rear-yard requirement beyond that), and apply them to the recorded measurements (the street lines meet at about 89.7 degrees and the lot reaches 144.60 ft from the corner point). Say which of the two existing engine answers the text supports: the older engine's geometry outputs 'not_required' (services/api/tests/scenario/three_answers/test_three_answers_benchmark.py, lines 176 to 178) while the decision module WITHHOLDS the rear yard (services/api/tests/scenario/three_answers/test_result_ways_benchmark.py: the lot reaches 144.60 ft from the corner point). Read the fixtures READ-ONLY; state plainly where the hand reading differs from what the program outputs today, and change NO program code and NO fixture: matching the program's saved output is not proof. THE OWNER'S STANDARDS this reading carries: every statement of what the law says quotes the captured text with its file and content digest; the reading is labelled an unreviewed draft with a link to the source text; where the text does not settle a point the reading says 'not sure' and names what would settle it; a figure from one dataset is a benchmark, not a rule; a missing fact stays unknown; legal limits are kept apart from practical estimates; a question of law is never turned into the owner's preference; and each worked example is worked by hand from the text, not matched to a program run. THE ZONING-RULE REVIEW REGISTER: this task changes no rule file and no program behaviour, so it adds no register entry and moves no revision. The register's GUIDE (docs/zoning-rule-review/GUIDE.md) covers the 23 implemented rule-definition files and moves a revision only on a change to a rule's interpretation, applicability, implementation or evidence; a reading written only into reference cases is none of these, and the human-verdict field is filled only by a named human and is not touched here. TESTS REQUIRED: one acceptance test per input state, with a table in the producer report; a red proof that a changed reading is caught; and one mutation proof per pinned branch (an unsettled row given a value is refused; a value where the two readings differ is refused; the older rows are superseded and the new targets stay current). NOT IN THIS TASK: the follow-up of the measurement-basis record (docs/measurement-basis/MEASUREMENT_BASIS.md still says 'not captured yet' for the mixed-building rule and the energy exclusion's eligibility, and its section 8a should record the owner's decisions of 2026-10-07) is a separate later task (DB-184 second piece); the parking/loading/bicycle LINE on the option display, the option comparison and the website (DB-180, R526/R548 display half); emitting contract 1.3.0 and carrying the legal unit limits into the results document (DB-185 a, c, d; DB-171, DB-172, DB-173, DB-175); adding a machine-readable condition field to reference rows (DB-175 a) and the consuming overlay-support test, which touches the scenario engine's tests and is deferred; any change to a rule file, the rule or scenario engine, a result, a capture, the review register or a plan; correcting the too-broad '30,000 sq ft' sentence in cases/interior-lots.json (DB-168 F1); and entering a human verdict anywhere.
business_reason: The owner's step 3 (R291) is to check the R6B answers with independently worked, source-backed examples. Forty-six official texts were captured by tasks M4-T033 and M4-T034 and have not been read into any reference case (DB-184): the mixed-building floor-area rule the owner's reviewer named (R513), the energy-exclusion eligibility definitions (R516), and the sections that decide whether parking, loading and bicycle parking apply to an option (R526, R548). Until these are read, the measurement-basis record stays out of date and no option can carry a resolved parking/loading/bicycle line. On the benchmark lot, one engine says the rear yard is not required and the decision module withholds it (DB-185 (b)); which is right is a reading of ZR 23-342 and 23-344, not a preference, and must be settled before any rear yard is shown.
